title: THE MARKET STAMP
front_challenge: I am going to [  ?  ] market tomorrow morning.
back_solution: I am going to THE market tomorrow morning.
rule: Specific physical destinations and municipal services take the definite article 'the' (the market, the station, the post office).
gag: "NO 'THE', NO ENTRY! Stamp approved, soldier! Next customer in line!"
thai_script: ไปตลาดพรุ่งนี้เช้า
thai_breakdown: ไป (M) = andare | ตลาด (L) = mercato | พรุ่งนี้ (H) = domani | เช้า (H) = mattina

title: THE 'TO' TOLL
front_challenge: I want [  ?  ] refactor this monolithic codebase.
back_solution: I want TO refactor this monolithic codebase.
rule: Verbs expressing intention, desire, or decision ('want', 'need', 'decide', 'hope') require the to-infinitive pattern.
gag: "ACCESS DENIED! Insert 'TO' token into the turnstile to ignite execution!"
thai_script: อยากปรับปรุงโค้ด
thai_breakdown: อยาก (L) = volere | ปรับปรุง (L-M) = migliorare/refactor | โค้ด (H) = codice

title: THE GERUND LIFE VEST
front_challenge: Always run the unit tests before [  ?  ] the pull request.
back_solution: Always run the unit tests before MERGING the pull request.
rule: Any verb following a preposition ('before', 'after', 'for', 'without', 'instead of') MUST take the gerund form (-ing).
gag: "MAN OVERBOARD! Verbs following prepositions drown without an -ING life vest!"
thai_script: ก่อนรวมโค้ด
thai_breakdown: ก่อน (L) = prima | รวม (M) = unire/merge | โค้ด (H) = codice

title: THE TIME PARADOX
front_challenge: Yesterday I [  ?  ] to the central market to buy fresh vegetables.
back_solution: Yesterday I WENT to the central market to buy fresh vegetables.
rule: Completed actions occurring in a closed, finished time frame ('yesterday', 'last year', 'two days ago') strictly require Past Simple.
gag: "TIME PARADOX DETECTED! 'Yesterday' is sealed in sector Past! Drop the present tense!"
thai_script: เมื่อวานไปตลาด
thai_breakdown: เมื่อวาน (F-M) = ieri | ไป (M) = andare | ตลาด (L) = mercato

title: THE LONE S-GUN
front_challenge: Every developer on our team [  ?  ] clean code practices.
back_solution: Every developer on our team FOLLOWS clean code practices.
rule: Third-person singular subjects and distributive determiners ('every', 'each', 'everyone') strictly demand a singular verb ending in '-s'.
gag: "REINFORCEMENTS! Singular subjects can't face production alone! Equip the '-S' carbine!"
thai_script: ทุกคนปฏิบัติตาม
thai_breakdown: ทุกคน (H-M) = ciascuno/tutti | ปฏิบัติตาม (L-L-L-M) = seguire le regole

title: THE DURATION CLOCK
front_challenge: She has been studying English [  ?  ] three years with Linguo.
back_solution: She has been studying English FOR three years with Linguo.
rule: Use 'for' to measure the total duration of an activity (three years, two hours); use 'since' to denote the starting point (2021, Monday).
gag: "TICK-TOCK! Measuring the whole time block? Hit 'FOR'! Pointing to the alarm start? Dial 'SINCE'!"
thai_script: เป็นเวลาสามปี
thai_breakdown: เป็นเวลา (M-M-M) = per la durata di | สาม (R) = tre | ปี (M) = anni

title: THE FACTORY PROTOCOL
front_challenge: Don't be afraid to [  ?  ] mistakes when practicing spoken English.
back_solution: Don't be afraid to MAKE mistakes when practicing spoken English.
rule: Use 'make' for creating, constructing, or producing results (make mistakes, make a decision); use 'do' for tasks, jobs, and general actions (do work, do research).
gag: "ASSEMBLY LINE ALERT! Mistakes are manufactured products! Engage the MAKE press!"
thai_breakdown: ทำ (M) = fare | ผิดพลาด (L-F) = commettere errori

title: THE GRAIN MEASURE
front_challenge: How [  ?  ] unit tests did you write for this module?
back_solution: How MANY unit tests did you write for this module?
rule: Use 'many' with plural countable nouns (tests, books, people); use 'much' with uncountable nouns (time, water, coffee, progress).
gag: "INVENTORY SCAN! Tests can be counted on your fingers! 'Much' will blow the capacitor!"
thai_script: กี่แบบทดสอบ
thai_breakdown: กี่ (L) = quanti | แบบทดสอบ (L-H-L) = test/prove

title: THE DISPATCH RECEIVER
front_challenge: The senior engineer [  ?  ] me to check the deployment logs.
back_solution: The senior engineer TOLD me to check the deployment logs.
rule: The verb 'tell' strictly requires a direct personal object (told me, told us); 'say' cannot take a direct personal object without 'to' (said to me).
gag: "TARGET LOCK ENGAGED! Recipient 'me' in the crosshairs? Only 'TELL/TOLD' has target tracking!"
thai_breakdown: บอก (L) = dire/informare | ฉัน (R) = me/io

title: THE EMOTION BATTERY
front_challenge: The lecture was very dense, so all the attendees felt [  ?  ].
back_solution: The lecture was very dense, so all the attendees felt BORED.
rule: Adjectives ending in '-ed' describe how a conscious person feels; adjectives ending in '-ing' describe the characteristic of the thing or event causing that feeling.
gag: "BATTERY CHARGE! The talk is boring, but humans absorb the '-ED' state! Don't call yourself an event!"
thai_script: รู้สึกเบื่อ
thai_breakdown: รู้สึก (H-L) = sentirsi | เบื่อ (L) = annoiato

title: THE RADAR SWEEP
front_challenge: Are you [  ?  ] debugging that concurrency issue?
back_solution: Are you STILL debugging that concurrency issue?
rule: Use 'still' to emphasize that a situation or action continues and is not finished; use 'already' to indicate completion earlier than expected.
gag: "RADAR SWEEP ACTIVE! Bug signal still emitting pulses? Keep the 'STILL' tracker locked!"
thai_script: ยังคงทำอยู่
thai_breakdown: ยังคง (M-M) = ancora/tuttora | ทำ (M) = fare | อยู่ (L) = particella continuativa

title: THE PROBABILITY GATE
front_challenge: If the test suite passes, we [  ?  ] deploy to production tonight.
back_solution: If the test suite passes, we WILL deploy to production tonight.
rule: In the First Conditional (realistic future possibility), the 'if' clause takes Present Simple and the main result clause takes 'will + bare infinitive'.
gag: "LOGIC GATE PASSED! Test condition true -> Ignite thrusters with 'WILL'!"
thai_script: ถ้าผ่านเราจะปล่อยระบบ
thai_phonetic: thâa phàan rao jà bplɔ̀y rá-bòp
thai_tones: F / L / M / L / L / H-L
thai_breakdown: ถ้า (F) = se | ผ่าน (L) = passa | เราจะ (M-L) = noi faremo | ปล่อยระบบ (L-H-L) = deploy sistema

title: THE RETRO TIMELINE
front_challenge: Before using automated pipelines, we [  ?  ] deploy manually via FTP.
back_solution: Before using automated pipelines, we USED TO deploy manually via FTP.
rule: Use 'used to + bare infinitive' for discontinued past routines and states; use 'be used to + gerund' for being accustomed to something in the present.
gag: "RETRO TIMELINE RESTORE! Ancient manual ritual detected! Load the 'USED TO' archive tape!"
thai_breakdown: เคย (M) = essere solito nel passato/aver fatto | ทำ (M) = fare

title: THE GRAVITY ANCHOR
front_challenge: The latency of the server depends [  ?  ] the network route.
back_solution: The latency of the server depends ON the network route.
rule: The verb 'depend' takes the dependent preposition 'on' (or 'upon'), never 'from' or 'of'.
gag: "GRAVITY LOCK MALFUNCTION! Romance-language false-friend detected! Clamp onto 'ON'!"
thai_script: ขึ้นอยู่กับเครือข่าย
thai_breakdown: ขึ้นอยู่กับ (F-L-L) = dipendere da | เครือข่าย (M-L) = rete

title: THE RATION GAUGE
front_challenge: Don't panic: we still have [  ?  ] minutes before the meeting starts.
back_solution: Don't panic: we still have A FEW minutes before the meeting starts.
rule: 'A few' has a positive nuance meaning 'some / a small amount'; bare 'few' emphasizes negative scarcity ('almost none').
gag: "RATION GAUGE READING! The letter 'A' breathes life! 'A few' gives hope; naked 'few' is starvation!"
thai_script: สองสามนาที
thai_breakdown: สองสาม (R-R) = due o tre / un po' di | นาที (M-M) = minuti
